basis.explanation: Historical successful ordering verified exact available runtime/type/version before boot, then booted and completed blocking bootstatus on that UUID before the120-second install. The completion consumer introduced additional postboot global-inventory/getenv reads that failed before installation. The coordinated patch restores the historical proof and ordering without claiming a postboot metadata read.

changes: Both retained completion consumers validate strict source-bound owned-device preboot metadata plus completed exact-UUID boot readiness, then retain the original120-second install.
Normal startup creates one uniquely named owned pinned Simulator first, uses bounded reads, preserves setup evidence and cleans only its exact UUID with20-second shutdown/delete budgets.

Normal audit requires the starter receipt, keeps actual host/toolchain/Mach-O/signature checks through bounded reads, retains combined compatibility evidence and prevents cases after a failed120-second iOS install.
Normal iOS installation and shell cleanup had no wall-time bound; the patch applies the existing reviewed consumer setup budgets to these operations.
The bounded helper preserves original timeouts when process-group cleanup is denied, records the denial and signals only its original live Popen child; no escalation or unbounded final wait.
Producer audit provenance now hashes all9 setup/runner/scenario inputs, including the starter, preboot verifier, bounded helper and shell.

Optional startup observation uses the public libproc API without launching ps, filters to allowlisted Simulator processes, rejects changed identities, retains before/after service metadata and never changes the command verdict.

verification.scope: Controlled source/runner regression tests; actual current app runtime acceptance is still required.
